User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the MPH Booking Central application.

role.description: Role of the user (e.g., teacher, unverified, admin).

SessionBooking.title: SessionBooking
SessionBooking.description: Represents a session booking in the MPH Booking Central application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the session booking.

teacherId.description: Reference to the teacher associated with this session. (Relationship: User 1:N SessionBooking)

programName.description: Name of the program for this session.

details.description: Additional details or notes about the session.

definition.description: Stores user information. Only the authenticated user (or admin, based on separate rules) can read/write their own document. This collection is used for authentication context. Should not be used for booking authorization. Roles are managed out of band.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user.

definition.description: Stores session booking information. Includes denormalized 'teacherId' for authorization independence. Teachers can only modify their own bookings.

params.name: bookingId
params.description: The unique identifier of the session booking.

firestore.reasoning:
This Firestore data structure is designed to support the MPH Booking Central application, focusing on secure access and efficient management of session bookings and user information. The structure emphasizes role-based access control (teacher, unverified, admin) and ensures that only authenticated users can access the data. Authentication Independence is achieved by storing the `teacherId` within the `SessionBooking` document. This enables rules to validate access without needing to read the User document.

**Authorization Independence:** The `teacherId` field in the `sessionBookings` collection denormalizes the user-session relationship, so rules can validate access based on the ID in the `request.auth.uid` without requiring a `get()` call to the `/users/{userId}` collection.

**Segregation:** All bookings are stored in a single collection (`sessionBookings`), enforcing a uniform security posture. Teachers can only modify bookings where their `id` matches the `teacherId` in the `sessionBookings` document. This aligns with the business rules, where admins would have broader access based on a separate rule (not defined here, as signup is disabled).

**Access Modeling:** The `sessionBookings` collection uses the `teacherId` to establish an owner-like relationship, meaning that a teacher can only edit session bookings related to them. There are no global roles (DBAC), as admin roles would be managed out of band.

**QAPs Support:** Using a single collection (`sessionBookings`) simplifies listing operations. A teacher can list all bookings where the `teacherId` matches their `uid` to display their sessions. The denormalization also ensures that listing operations can be secured without additional `get()` calls.
